items.title: Uniform vanishing of a Tor map in the degree of an upper bound for the number of generators of the ideal
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file local-cohomology.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is a uniformity assertion with no further hypothesis on the module: above the degree given by an upper bound t for the number of generators of the ideal, the Tor maps between two powers of the ideal vanish for all modules and all sufficiently large exponents, with constants depending only on the ideal (author lemma at source lines 4713-4722, label lemma-tor-maps-vanish). The proof (source lines 4724-4785) is a descending induction on an invariant of the module that counts the generators whose fixed power already acts as zero, with the base case supplied by the vanishing lemma for modules annihilated by a power of the ideal and the induction step organised around the exact sequence of the kernel and the quotient of multiplication by that power; the two end terms have strictly larger invariant and the conclusion is read off from a diagram of Tor modules with one arrow zero by construction (proof lines 4764-4784). The invariant, the induction and the sandwiching are the content; the author closes with the standard remark that routine details are omitted. H3.
